Mills-ratio bounds (Lemma 2.2): x phi(x)/(1 + x^2) <= Q(x) <= phi(x)/x give phi(z) <= Q(z)(z + 1/z) and phi(z)/Q(z) >= z, so e^(-z^2/2) = sqrt(2 pi) phi(z) <= sqrt(pi/2) p (z + 1/z) and it suffices that u(z) = -ln p - c(z + 1/z) >= 0 (page's steps; -ln p = -ln 2 - ln Q, Q' = -phi, so u' = phi/Q - c(1 - 1/z^2)). u' >= z - c(1 - 1/z^2) > 0 for all z > 0 (for z < 1 the right side is negative; for z >= 1 it is below c < 1 <= z), so u is increasing. At p = 1/e, z* = 0.9004526 and u(z*) = 1 - c(z* + 1/z*) = 0.0727888 > 0 (scipy). The page's displayed arithmetic 1 - 0.46107 x 2.01101 = 0.0728 (exact 0.072789 -> 0.0728). For 0 < p <= 1/e, z >= z* so u(z) >= u(z*) > 0. Numerical check on p in (0, 1/e] (200,000 points): min of (-e p ln p - e^(-z^2/2)) = +3.1e-5 > 0; the inequality fails above 1/e (checked on [0.6, 0.99]). PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html Lab 6 hypothesis (line 722) and interpretation (line 873): 'On the same bootstrap draws, a maximum over more rules is at least as large, so every family-wide critical value below is at most the one the full search would need'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: Re-derived. Fix the bootstrap draws (the same index vectors). For rule sets A subset of A', the max over A' of the centred t*_k is pointwise at least the max over A. Hence the (1 - alpha) quantile over the draws of the max over A' is at least that over A, so a critical value computed on the 30 rules is at most the one for any larger universe (and StepM's step-1 critical value is non-decreasing in the number of rules). The argument uses only the definition of the maximum and of the empirical quantile. Numerical check (subset_quantile.py; the twin's draws: seed 507, mean block 10, B = 1000): the 95% quantile of the max of the centred t* over the first m rules is 2.1404 (m = 5), 2.4525 (10), 2.6475 (15), 2.8040 (20), 2.8178 (25) and 2.8371 (all 30; this is the twin's StepM first step, 2.837). No violation over the 29 nested prefixes. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html lines 596-598 (equicorrelated normals are MTP2 for 0 <= rho < 1; one-sided p-values; the Simes step at line 598), Lab 5 hypothesis (line 638)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: Re-derived at d10fb51. (a) Sigma = (1-rho) I + rho 11' with Sherman-Morrison: Sigma^{-1} = (1/(1-rho)) [I - rho 11'/(1-rho+m0 rho)], so the off-diagonal entries of Q are -rho/((1-rho)(1-rho+m0 rho)) <= 0 for 0 <= rho < 1. (b) For a normal density with precision Q, log f(z) = const - (1/2) z'Qz; with u = x v y and v = x ^ y, u_i^2 + v_i^2 = x_i^2 + y_i^2, so the diagonal terms cancel and log f(u) + log f(v) - log f(x) - log f(y) = (1/2) sum_{i != j} Q_ij (x_i x_j + y_i y_j - u_i u_j - v_i v_j). The bracket is 0 when (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) >= 0 and equals (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) <= 0 otherwise (checked in the four sign cases), so each term Q_ij times the bracket is >= 0 and f(u) f(v) >= f(x) f(y). Numerical spot check (num/simes_mtp2_check.out): 200,000 random pairs for each of (m, rho) = (3, 0.2), (5, 0.7), (10, 0.95), (20, 0): min(lhs - rhs) = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, -1.4e-14 (rounding), violations 0. (c) One-sided p-values are decreasing in z coordinatewise, which swaps join and meet, and the Jacobian is a product of one-coordinate factors that cancels because {u_i, v_i} = {x_i, y_i}: the true-null p-values are MTP2 as the page says. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html Proposition 7.8 and proof (lines 600-607)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: Re-derived after the rename A -> D. If the original procedure makes no false rejection, the augmented procedure rejects R = R0 + D' with D' = min(D, m - R0) <= D, at most D' of them false; R = 0 gives FDP = 0; otherwise FDP <= D'/(R0 + D') <= D/(R0 + D) because x -> x/(R0 + x) is increasing; and D <= gamma R0/(1 - gamma) iff D (1 - gamma) <= gamma R0 iff D <= gamma (R0 + D), so FDP <= gamma. Hence {FDP > gamma} needs a false rejection by the original procedure: probability <= alpha. Correct, and the letters D, D' no longer clash with the active set A.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html line 598 (new T span: 'In this design the Simes inequality also follows from Lesson 3 alone'); Lesson 3 Definition 5.1, Theorem 5.2, Proposition 5.3 (course/modules/S/S7/L03.html lines 262-282); Theorem 7.5 (L05.html lines 559-571)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: Derivation, written out and checked: (1) Lab 5's true-null statistics are z_j = sqrt(rho) W + sqrt(1-rho) eps_j with mu_j = 0 (the lab code: z = sqrt(rho) w + sqrt(1-rho) e + mu), p_j = 1 - Phi(z_j), rho in [0,1): this is Proposition 5.3's model restricted to the nulls, so the true-null p-values are PRDS on every subset (Definition 5.1). (2) Theorem 5.2's hypotheses hold for the family of the m0 true-null p-values (the family is all true nulls, so PRDS on the true nulls is PRDS on the family; each p_j is super-uniform because z_j ~ N(0,1) gives p_j ~ U(0,1); P(p_j <= u) = u > 0 for u > 0). Its bound FDR <= m0' q / m' with m' = m0' = m0 gives FDR <= q = alpha for BH at level alpha on the family. (3) When every hypothesis in the family is true, V = R, so FDR = E[1{R >= 1}] = P(R >= 1). (4) BH at level alpha on m0 p-values (step-up) rejects at least one hypothesis iff q_(l) <= l alpha/m0 for some l <= m0. Hence P(union_{l<=m0} {q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}) <= alpha: the Simes inequality for the true-null p-values. (5) Theorem 7.5 (containment {FDP > gamma} subset of union_{l<=M}{q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}, M <= m0, for the step-down with constants (3)) gives P(FDP > gamma) <= alpha for every rho in [0,1). Numerical check (num/simes_mtp2_check.py, seeded; output num/simes_mtp2_check.out): union frequency for m0 = 20, 100, 450 and rho = 0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 0.95 is between 0.0163 and 0.0508 (the largest, 0.0508 +- 0.0011 at m0 = 450, rho = 0, is the independent case where the Simes bound is exact at alpha; the difference from 0.05 is 0.7 se); BH any-rejection and the Simes union agree on the same draws (0.036 and 0.036, rho 0.5, m0 30). 'Bonferroni, Holm and BHY treat every hypothesis alike' follows from Definition 2.1 and the step-down and step-up rules (the procedures use the p-values only through their ranks and the values of the statistics; the threshold of Bonferroni is the same at every step). 'Neither holds exactly for small samples, fat tails or serially correlated predictor returns' is a statement about the asymptotic normal approximation (Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.3 are asymptotic in the normal approximation; the MBF formula assumes the normal test statistic). Neither is an empirical or literature claim, so neither needs a span under the page's convention, and neither carries a number. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html Definition 6.6 (lines 491-496) and the paragraph at line 499: 'Since V/max(R,1) <= 1{V >= 1}, any simultaneous band at level 1 - alpha, restricted to any selection, has FCR <= alpha'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: Re-derived: for every outcome, V/max(R,1) <= 1{V >= 1} (if V = 0 both sides are 0; if V >= 1 then R >= V >= 1, so V/R <= 1). Hence FCR = E[V/max(R,1)] <= P(V >= 1) for any selection rule. If the band covers every mean simultaneously with probability >= 1 - alpha, then V = 0 on that event, so P(V >= 1) <= alpha, which gives FCR <= alpha. Numerical spot-check (numpy, /home/user/quant-phd/.claude/worktrees/verify62/.venv, seed 29, 200000 replications): K = 20 independent N(0,1) estimates, the Bonferroni band with critical value Phi^-1(1 - alpha/(2K)) = 3.0233, and selection rules 'the R largest |z|' for R = 1, 3, 10, 20; the largest simulated FCR is 0.0488 <= 0.05. The line-499 text is unchanged apart from the marker. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html Theorem 7.4 (line 543, statement and proof lines 544-551), display (2)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: Re-derived the two facts the proof uses. (a) alpha_i of (2) is nondecreasing in i: for i <= k it equals k alpha/m, and for i > k it equals k alpha/(m + k - i), which grows with i and equals k alpha/m at i = k. (b) For i = m - m_0 + k > k (when m_0 < m), k alpha/(m + k - i) = k alpha/m_0, the identity behind 'q_(k) <= alpha_j <= alpha_{m-m_0+k} = k alpha/m_0'. Numerical check (python, exhaustive over 1 <= k <= m < 60 and alpha in {0.05, 0.1}, all m_0 in [k, m]): nondecreasing and identity both hold (True). The Theorem's conclusion is Theorem 2.2 of Lehmann and Romano (R29-arxiv-lehmann2005generalizations). PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html display (3) (line 557) and the 'nondecreasing' sentence after it
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: Derived: with k = floor(gamma i) + 1 in display (2), the constant is (floor(gamma i)+1) alpha/(m + floor(gamma i) + 1 - i), which is display (3). Since gamma < 1, floor(gamma i) < i, so k <= i, and (2)'s second case applies except at i = k, where both cases give k alpha/m; so (3) is (2) with that k. From i to i+1, floor(gamma i) rises by 0 or 1, so the numerator does not fall and the denominator m + floor(gamma i) + 1 - i does not rise: nondecreasing. Numerical check (python, m in {5, 20, 50, 500}, gamma in {0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99}, alpha = 0.05): (3) equals (2) with k = floor(gamma i)+1 for every i, k <= i, and (3) is nondecreasing (True). PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html key-results table, row 4 (raw line 534; grade T; source 'Proved in §3; Lab 2'): 'Reporting the best of K independent null analyses gives a false-positive rate 1-(1-alpha)^K under independence; under any dependence it lies between alpha and min(1,K alpha) (Proposition 3.2)'
rows.evidence: Proposition 3.2 (L06 lines 171-177) states exactly these two results: (i) independent p-values: P(min_k P_k <= alpha) = 1-(1-alpha)^K, with min_k P_k ~ Beta(1,K); (ii) dependent p-values: alpha <= P(min_k P_k <= alpha) <= min(1, K alpha). Re-derived by hand: P(min_k P_k > u) = (1-u)^K under independence, the Beta(1,K) cdf, mean 1/(K+1); the lower bound follows from {min <= alpha} containing {P_1 <= alpha}, with P(P_1 <= alpha) = alpha for uniform p-values; the upper bound is the union bound. Numerical spot-check (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify62h-L05-L06/r32/num/prop32_mc.py -> prop32_mc.out; numpy seed 20261021; 400,000 equicorrelated two-sided z-tests per row, exact size 5%): K = 36: rho = 0 -> 0.8412 (SE 0.0006) against 1-0.95^36 = 0.8422; rho = 0.5 -> 0.5477; rho = 0.9 -> 0.1801; rho = 0.99 -> 0.0792; all inside [0.05, 1]. K = 2: 0.0975, 0.0906, 0.0703, 0.0570, all inside [0.05, 0.10]. The removed clause 'shared data lowers it toward alpha' is not claimed for K analyses by the proposition; the row now states what the proposition proves. Grade T is correct (proved on the page). PASS.

rows.evidence: The published-factors clause is replaced by a conditional example ('as when a study reports only t-statistics, without the returns behind them'). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html line 351 (Section 5): 'Under positive dependence it widens, because StepM's critical values fall toward the one-test value 1.645 as correlation approaches one, while Holm's do not move.'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: A qualitative consequence, weaker than the inequality on line 333 (R31-L05-line333-never-favours). Checkable parts: Holm's thresholds Phi^-1(1 - alpha/a) depend only on the number of active hypotheses, not on dependence (Definition 1.2 and the Holm identity stated on the page); StepM's critical value falls toward the one-test value 1.645 as the variants become identical (Lab 3's joint critical value 1.601 against the benchmark 1.645; E1 at rho = 0.9 gives 2.173, and its solution says 'should approach the one-test value 1.645 from above'). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html line 512 (Section 7 opening: 'With hundreds or thousands of candidates, demanding that not one claim be false sacrifices most true discoveries (§9)') and line 883 (Section 9: 'Demanding that not even one of thousands of claims is false sacrifices most true discoveries.')
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: A qualitative power statement with a design behind it. Lab 5 (its twin at m = 500 equicorrelated one-sided tests, 50 real effects of mean 3, q = 0.10, 1000 replications; the embedded block reproduced digit for digit, labs/lab-S7-L05-5.out) prints, for rho = 0.0, 0.5, 0.8: Holm with augmentation finds 14.34, 13.97, 14.46 of the 50 real effects against 36.17, 33.19, 33.30 for BH (q = 0.1) and 8.98, 9.80, 11.22 for the corrected constants (LR(26)/C). So FWER-type control keeps under a third of the true effects in this design, which supports 'most'. The sentence says 'hundreds or thousands'; Lab 5 uses m = 500 (hundreds), and the 'thousands' case is the same direction (Holm and Bonferroni thresholds rise with m), not a computed number. Grade C would apply if the sentence were a key result; it is an interpretive remark on Lab 5. PASS. Round 32: the lab scenario text is unchanged; re-read at 0b0dbe0.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html line 180 (Section 3): 'Real specification searches sit between the two bounds, because the analyses share data.'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 7a0d063 (git diff checked); round-31 evidence: Under a true null, Proposition 3.2 gives alpha <= P(min P_k <= alpha) <= min(1, K alpha) for dependent p-values; the independent value 1-(1-alpha)^K lies inside those bounds. A search whose analyses share data is dependent, so it sits between the bounds. The 'because' names the premise (shared data); it is a derivation on the page, not a literature claim. PASS.
